title: Multiple failed MFA attempts followed by successful login
description: User finance.manager@company.com received 18 failed MFA prompts from an unfamiliar IP, followed by a successful login from a new device in another country.

title: Suspicious PowerShell execution with encoded command
description: powershell.exe executed with -EncodedCommand from a workstation. Decoded content attempted to download and run a script from an external domain.

title: Login from unusual location
description: Employee logged in from Singapore after normally authenticating only from India. MFA was successful, but the device fingerprint is new.

title: EC2 instance communicating with known malicious IP
description: An EC2 instance initiated outbound HTTPS traffic to an IP address associated with command-and-control infrastructure.

title: Known IT inventory tool flagged as suspicious
description: An internal asset inventory executable triggered suspicious behavior detection, but the binary is signed and matches the approved software hash.

title: User reported suspicious email
description: A user reported an email containing a link to a newly registered domain. The sender domain fails DMARC alignment.

title: Repeated failed login from known employee device
description: User failed password login 3 times and then successfully authenticated from the same trusted laptop and office IP.

title: Large outbound data transfer to unknown host
description: Database server transferred 9.8 GB to an external IP over HTTPS outside business hours. Destination is not in the approved vendor list.

title: Risky sign-in from anonymous proxy
description: User authenticated successfully from an IP associated with an anonymous proxy service. The user normally signs in from a managed corporate device.

title: Internal development server running outdated TLS
description: An internal-only development server still accepts TLS 1.1. The host is isolated from production data and has no internet exposure.

title: Outbound connection to newly observed domain
description: Workstation initiated HTTPS traffic to a domain registered 5 days ago. Domain is not categorized and has no known business owner.

title: Large file upload to personal cloud storage
description: User uploaded 1.8 GB of files to a personal Google Drive account. Files include spreadsheet names matching customer export patterns.

title: Public storage bucket containing sensitive file names
description: A cloud storage bucket was changed to public-read. Object names include payroll_export and customer_backup references.

title: Mass file rename with ransomware-like extension
description: Endpoint renamed 2,900 files in 5 minutes and created recovery note files in multiple directories. Shadow copy deletion was attempted and blocked.

title: Marketing email reported as phishing by one user
description: One user reported a vendor newsletter as phishing. SPF, DKIM, and DMARC passed, links point to the vendor's legitimate domain, and no other users reported it.

title: New local administrator account created
description: A local admin account was created on a file server after business hours. No matching change ticket was found.

title: Periodic beacon-like outbound traffic
description: A workstation contacted the same external host every 60 seconds for 4 hours. Destination has low reputation but is not present on known blocklists.

title: Firewall rule change matches approved ticket
description: A firewall rule was added during the approved maintenance window and matches change ticket CHG-8841.

title: Service account reading above baseline
description: Application service account read 15 times its usual daily row count from the customer table. A batch export was scheduled, but normally uses a different service account.

title: Mass mailbox export after MFA method change
description: User initiated export of executive mailbox data 4 hours after changing MFA phone number from an unfamiliar IP address.

title: Scheduled vulnerability scan detected as port scan
description: Sequential TCP connections were generated by the approved scanner during the weekly scanning window.

title: Unsigned binary executed from Downloads folder
description: Unsigned executable launched from a user's Downloads folder. No malware signature matched, but the file was downloaded from an untrusted domain.

title: VPN impossible travel false positive
description: User appeared to log in from two countries within 10 minutes, but the second IP belongs to the corporate VPN egress range.

title: SQL injection pattern blocked
description: WAF blocked multiple requests containing SQL injection payloads against the login endpoint. Source IP belongs to a residential ISP and attempted several paths.

title: Web shell signature detected on public server
description: A file matching known web shell patterns was created in a public web upload directory. Web server process spawned a command shell shortly afterward.

title: New SaaS domain queried from onboarding channel
description: Workstation queried a newly registered SaaS help domain after the user clicked a link posted by HR in the onboarding channel.

title: Access key used from unfamiliar country
description: A production IAM access key was used from a country never seen before for this account. The action listed S3 buckets and security groups.

title: Large print job from finance user
description: Finance user printed a 280-page quarterly report during month-end close. Document template and user role match expected business activity.

title: DCSync-like replication request from workstation
description: A non-domain-controller workstation issued replication-style requests shortly after a privileged account logged in interactively.

title: Managed device temporarily out of compliance
description: Laptop missed one disk encryption status check but reported compliant again on the next sync 12 minutes later.

title: Live cloud credential committed to a public repository
description: Secret scanning flagged an AWS access key with production IAM permissions committed to a public fork of the payments-service repo. The key has not yet been rotated.

title: Unapproved dependency added to release pipeline
description: A new npm package was added to the deploy pipeline for the checkout service hours before a release, published by an account with no prior history and no code review approval.

title: Container process attempted to access host filesystem
description: A pod in the staging namespace executed a shell that attempted to mount the host's root filesystem. Image was pulled from an internal registry but is not on the approved base-image list.

title: IAM role grants overly broad S3 permissions
description: A newly created IAM role for the analytics team includes s3:* on all buckets instead of the requested read-only scope on two buckets. No production incident has occurred yet.

title: Critical CVE detected in production container image
description: A base image running in production includes a library with a critical remote-code-execution CVE disclosed 2 days ago. A patched image is available upstream.

title: Unusual internal SMB scanning between subnets
description: A finance-floor workstation initiated SMB connection attempts to over 40 hosts in the engineering subnet within 3 minutes, a pattern with no prior baseline for this device.

title: DNS query to typosquatted domain of internal SSO provider
description: A workstation queried 'corp-0kta-login.com', a lookalike domain registered last week, shortly after the user received an email referencing a login issue.

title: Credential stuffing attempt blocked by bot detection
description: Over 400 login attempts using leaked credential pairs were blocked in 10 minutes by automated bot-detection rules. No account reached a successful authentication.

title: Invoice fraud attempt impersonating known vendor
description: An email impersonating the finance contact at an existing vendor requested an urgent change to bank routing details. Reply-to address does not match the vendor's verified domain.

title: Managed Mac reports jailbreak/tamper indicators
description: A company-managed MacBook reported MDM profile removal followed by installation of a known jailbreak tool, then went offline from device management.

title: Third-party OAuth app granted broad mailbox access
description: A user granted a low-reputation third-party app full read/send access to their corporate mailbox via 'Sign in with Google'. The app is not on the approved SaaS list.

title: Mass file access anomaly ahead of typical ransomware pattern
description: A service account began sequentially opening and closing thousands of files across two file shares over 90 seconds, matching a known ransomware staging pattern rather than an approved backup job.

title: Volumetric DDoS attempt auto-mitigated at edge
description: A short-lived volumetric attack against the public marketing site was automatically absorbed by edge rate-limiting; origin servers saw no traffic increase and no downtime occurred.

title: Synthetic monitoring alert during approved maintenance window
description: An uptime check fired for the billing API, but the outage window matches an approved change ticket for a scheduled database migration.

title: Customer PII pasted into a public Slack channel
description: A support engineer pasted a spreadsheet snippet containing customer emails and phone numbers into a public support channel; the message was auto-flagged and not yet deleted.

title: Prompt injection attempt against internal support assistant
description: A support ticket contained hidden text instructing the internal AI assistant to ignore its guardrails and reveal other customers' account data. The assistant refused, but the attempt was logged.

title: Third-party SaaS vendor disclosed a data breach
description: A vendor used for customer support ticketing sent a breach notification indicating access-token exposure. The vendor is integrated with the production support queue.

title: Badge used at two office locations within an implausible time window
description: An employee's badge was used to enter the Mumbai office and, 12 minutes later, the Bengaluru office 1,000 km away. No travel record or badge-sharing exception is on file.

title: Confidential document printed matches normal role activity
description: A legal team member printed a confidential contract draft after hours; the user's role and document type match established quarter-end contract review patterns.

title: Malicious browser extension installed on managed endpoint
description: A browser extension installed outside the approved store manifest was observed exfiltrating form-fill data to an external domain before being auto-quarantined by the isolation agent.

title: Spike in API key usage matches confirmed partner integration launch
description: A partner's API key exceeded its historical rate limit by 6x, but the spike coincides with a scheduled go-live for a new integration confirmed by the partnerships team.

title: Suspected synthetic-voice vishing call to finance team
description: A finance analyst received a call using a voice closely matching the CFO requesting an urgent wire transfer. Call originated from a VoIP number never associated with the CFO, and the request bypassed normal approval channels.

title: Unauthorized force-push to protected release branch
description: The 'release/prod' branch, which requires two approving reviews, was force-pushed using an admin override outside business hours, rewriting the last 6 commits.

title: Critical patch auto-remediated within SLA after missed window
description: A workstation missed its scheduled patch window due to being offline, then automatically installed the critical security update on next check-in, within the 48-hour SLA.

title: Departing employee downloaded unusual volume of sales data
description: An employee who submitted resignation notice 2 days ago downloaded the entire regional sales pipeline export, a report they do not normally access.

title: Fileless malware injected into legitimate system process
description: A reflective DLL injection was detected into explorer.exe on a finance workstation moments after a macro-enabled document was opened from an email attachment.

title: Push MFA approved from newly re-provisioned corporate device
description: A user approved a push MFA prompt from a device that was freshly re-imaged by IT that morning per an open helpdesk ticket; device posture and network match expected values.

title: DNS tunneling pattern detected on guest network segment
description: A device on the guest Wi-Fi segment issued abnormally long, high-entropy TXT record queries at a steady interval, consistent with DNS tunneling rather than normal browsing.

title: SIM-swap indicator flagged during customer support verification
description: A customer support call requested an account recovery for a number that was ported to a new carrier 40 minutes earlier, a pattern strongly correlated with SIM-swap fraud.

title: Kubernetes RBAC change matches approved infrastructure ticket
description: A new ClusterRoleBinding granting deploy permissions to the CI service account was applied during the maintenance window and matches change ticket INF-4471.
